All three test classes compile and run; 74 of 75 tests pass. One test fails, and it reveals a real bug.

**Bug found:** `WriteableCommandLineImplAgentTest.testAddOptionFullyRegistersAncestorsForTriggerLookup`

In `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)` (`src/java/org/apache/commons/cli2/commandline/WriteableCommandLineImpl.java:67-81`), the loop that climbs the parent chain (`// ensure that all parent options are also added`) only appends ancestor options to the internal `options` list, making `hasOption(ancestor)` return `true`. It never registers the ancestor's preferred name/triggers in `nameToOption`, so `getOption(ancestor.getPreferredName())` returns `null` for an option the command line itself reports as present. The comment's intent ("ensure that all parent options are also added") implies the ancestor should be as fully registered as if `addOption(ancestor)` had been called directly, but it isn't — `hasOption()` and `getOption()` become inconsistent for ancestor options added only implicitly via child climbing.

All other tests (including boundary/error cases like `addSwitch` called twice, `validate()` with too few/too many options, `getOptions()`/`getAnonymous()` immutability, `looksLikeOption` with no prefixes, defaults propagation, nested `findOption`, and `process()` halting on an unrecognized token) passed, confirming the rest of the behavior matches the documented contract.
